key_insight: QDIFF tests quantum software stacks by comparing output distributions across semantically equivalent program variants.
engineering_relevance: It targets correctness across quantum languages, compilers, simulators, and hardware execution while reducing costly hardware tests.
method: Generate program variants using semantics-preserving source-to-source transformations.
Filter circuits before hardware execution using depth, two-qubit operations, gate error rates, and T1 relaxation time.
Check distribution equivalence using extensible comparisons such as Kolmogorov–Smirnov tests and cross entropy.
evidence_signal: The abstract describes the testing approach but reports no benchmark sizes, bug counts, or measured speedups.
watch_item: Statistical comparisons must account for sampling variability and hardware noise to avoid flagging expected variation as software defects.
paper_title: QDiff: Differential Testing of Quantum Software Stacks
